description: Exposure, credentials, and tool authorization. MCP rules stay advisory deliberately: promoting them while the approval-gating asymmetry is unresolved would encode the current posture as the intended one. See ADR-003.

rules.statement: The base stack publishes zero host ports; the dev stack binds only to 127.0.0.1; production publishes only the Traefik entrypoints plus a loopback dashboard; data-internal stays internal.
rules.rationale: This is the real security posture, and it is per-stack. A generic host-port-conflict check is near-vacuous against a base file that publishes nothing, while a dev port moved from loopback to 0.0.0.0 exposes a developer's database to their network and would pass such a check.
rules.promotion_criteria: The Compose extractor lands and the assertion runs clean across all four stacks. This is a strong promotion candidate: the condition is objective and the current tree already satisfies it.

rules.statement: Every third-party image is pinned by SHA256 digest.
rules.rationale: Already true of every image in all four Compose files. The rule prevents regression rather than requesting a change.
rules.promotion_criteria: The Compose extractor lands. Promote quickly: the current tree is fully compliant, so a violation is unambiguously new.

rules.statement: Secret variables are declared and classified, and no governance artifact ever contains a secret value.
rules.rationale: Governance reads the whole repository, so anything it writes is a potential exfiltration path.

rules.statement: Secret status comes from the curated classification list, never inferred from a field's type.
rules.rationale: Secret fields are inconsistently typed here: GOOGLE_API_CLIENT_SECRET is a SecretStr while GOOGLE_CLIENT_SECRET is a plain string. Any type-based rule would miss the second one and report confidently.
rules.promotion_criteria: The configuration extractor lands and every secret in the tree is classified.

rules.statement: The GitHub MCP tool allowlist is identical across the container flags, the settings-validator frozenset, and the runtime post-probe assert.
rules.rationale: Three independent enforcement layers is good defence and a good drift surface. Widening one layer only is the exact failure this catches; governance cross-checks the three rather than adding a fourth declaration.
rules.promotion_criteria: The MCP extractor lands and the three-layer comparison runs clean.

rules.statement: Widening an MCP tool allowlist, or adding a write-capable tool source, requires explicit human approval recorded in a change record.
rules.rationale: Automation may propose this and may not decide it.
rules.promotion_criteria: Cannot be promoted to an automated check: the judgement is the point. It becomes enforceable only as a review requirement.

rules.statement: Every governance surface strips query strings and userinfo from a connection URL before storing, logging, or emitting it.
rules.rationale: The catalog supports placing a token in the URL. Since 2026-08-20 the application stores the url column credential-stripped and keeps the full URL Fernet-encrypted in connect_url (migration 0029), but a URL in flight is still credential-bearing until proven otherwise, so every governance surface strips before it stores or logs.

rules.statement: A write-capable tool is approval-gated regardless of whether it is sourced from the Google REST executor or from an MCP server.
rules.rationale: Holds since 2026-08-20: every user-added MCP toolset is wrapped in ApprovalRequiredToolset, pausing any tool not annotated readOnlyHint for the same deferred-tool approval flow the Google write tools use. Fail-closed — an unannotated tool is treated as a mutation. Deployment-managed servers stay outside the gate because their explicit allowed_tools lists are curated and enforced at startup.
rules.promotion_criteria: Promote once an automated check asserts that every per-user spec built by build_toolsets_for_user carries require_approval. Today the guarantee is held by backend-unit (tests/test_mcp_connections.py TestApprovalGating and TestToolsetsForUser).

rules.statement: A stored connection URL is revalidated at probe and attach time, not only when it is written.
rules.rationale: Holds since 2026-08-20: user-connection specs carry revalidate_url, so every turn re-runs the SSRF/DNS check ahead of the probe cache before the toolset attaches, and the connection test endpoint revalidates before probing. Deployment-managed sidecars are exempt (they resolve internally by design). Residual: DNS is re-resolved by the HTTP client at connect, so a sub-second rebinding race remains; network-level egress controls stay the preferred hardening.
rules.promotion_criteria: Promote once an automated check asserts the revalidation call sits in front of the probe cache. Today the guarantee is held by backend-unit (tests/test_mcp_connections.py TestConnectionTimeRevalidation).

rules.statement: Every frontend MCP catalog entry maps to a backend kind or to documented generic handling.
rules.rationale: A catalog entry with no backend mapping is a connection the interface offers and the executor does not recognize.
rules.promotion_criteria: The catalog extractor lands and the mapping is complete.

rules.statement: Governance tooling never imports app.* in-process.
rules.rationale: Settings loading walks parent directories for .env and main.py configures Logfire at import scope, so an in-process import can load real secrets and emit telemetry from a tool that only means to read files.
